## Context / Problem

`examples/agent-skills/rebar-debug/SKILL.md` Step 7, Axis 1 "Class review" item 1 (introduced by story dff2-9c38-c454-4daa) **unconditionally** mandates that every confirmed sibling class add "one criterion asserting a structural check over the class (a construct-uniqueness guard, or an equivalent that fails if a new instance appears)". Mandating a structural guard for *every* class that has >= 1 sibling over-produces guards: it invites CI bloat, standing maintenance burden, and change-detector checks for classes whose re-entry risk a plain regression test already covers. The skill has no guidance for *when* a guard is warranted or *how* to design one that survives refactors and stays portable.

This follow-on (requested by the operator this session) converts that unconditional mandate into a bright-line evaluation, backed by a new conditionally-loaded companion prompt, `structural-guards.md`, mirroring how `test-design.md` and `llm-behavioral-taxonomy.md` are loaded on demand.

## Scope (documentation only -- no code, no ticket-system change)

- `examples/agent-skills/rebar-debug/structural-guards.md` (NEW) -- the companion prompt.
- `examples/agent-skills/rebar-debug/SKILL.md` -- Step 7 Axis-1 item 1 flips from the unconditional guard mandate to a decision routed through `structural-guards.md`.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Step 7 item 1 contains no unconditional structural-check mandate; it routes the decision through `structural-guards.md`. Verified by reading item 1 and by `tests/unit/test_rebar_debug_step7_class_review.py` returning exit 0.
- [ ] Step 7 item 1 still requires one acceptance-criterion checkbox per confirmed sibling naming its path and symbol. Verified by reading item 1.
- [ ] `examples/agent-skills/rebar-debug/structural-guards.md` is present. Verified by `test -f`.
- [ ] `structural-guards.md` opens with a header naming what it governs and its load points (rebar-debug Step 7 Axis 1; rebar-implement). Verified by reading the header.
- [ ] `structural-guards.md` states the WHEN decision as numbered questions phrased as affirmative tests. Verified by reading the "does this class earn a guard" section.
- [ ] `structural-guards.md` contains a portability table mapping bug shape to guard shape across at least four enforcement layers. Verified by reading the table.
- [ ] `structural-guards.md` enumerates the design properties as affirmative statements (match on structure not text; carry intent inline; binary and blocking; survive refactor; ship a true-negative). Verified by reading the properties section.
- [ ] `scripts/check_skill_frontmatter.py` returns exit 0 and `tests/unit/test_skill_shared_sync.py` returns exit 0 (the new companion needs no frontmatter and is not a shared-synced file). Verified by running each.

## Test plan

Documentation change. Run: `python scripts/check_skill_frontmatter.py`; `python -m pytest tests/unit/test_rebar_debug_step7_class_review.py tests/unit/test_skill_shared_sync.py tests/unit/test_check_skill_frontmatter.py`; `make lint`. No runtime behavior changes.

## Attribution

Additive skill enhancement, not a defect fix -- it evolves the Step-7 directive that story dff2-9c38-c454-4daa shipped. Relates-to dff2 and its epic e71b (bug-trend program: debug-skill upgrades).
